senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. preced. wds) to jest, mock.
units: <cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 34:1">Pesik. R. s. 34</cite> <he>לשוא לָעַגְנוּ על וכ׳</he> in vain did we deride their words.

senses.gloss: <cite ref="L00594">same</cite>. Y. Peah I, 15ᵈ top (ref. to <cite ref="Proverbs 30:17">Prov. XXX, 17</cite>) <he>עין שהִלְעִיגָה על וכ׳</he> the eye that mocked at the law commanding to honor father and mother and despised the law (<cite ref="Deuteronomy 22:6">Deut. XXII, 6</cite>) &c.
units: <cite ref="Eruvin 21b:11">Erub. 21ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="L00157"><he>להג</he></cite>, <cite ref="Ecclesiastes 12:12">Koh. XII, 12</cite>) <he>כל המַלְעִיג על וכ׳</he> whosoever derides the words of the wise, v. <cite ref="L00597"><he>לַעַג</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 94">Gen. R. s. 94</cite> <he>מַלְעִיגִים בשפתותיהן</he> spoke lasciviously.
<cite ref="Esther Rabbah 6:1">Esth. R. to III, 9</cite> <he>מַלְעִיגִין אותנו וכ׳</he> they deride us and our religion.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 16:8">Num. R. s. 16</cite> <he>הִלְעִיגוּ לי</he> they spoke irreverently of me. Y. Naz. I, beg. 51ᵃ [read:] <he>מהו זה מַלְעִיג עליהן או וכ׳</he> how is this? Does he mean it sarcastically, or does he mean to say, I will be a Nazir like them? <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 250:1">Yalk. Ex. 250</cite> <he>ורוה״ק מַלְעֶגֶת עליו</he> and the Spirit of Holiness laughs at him; a. e.
